title: Email/query smtp path: full ID scan before pagination
description:
In the Email/query handler (server.rs ~line 581), when the requested mailbox is a special folder (e.g. INBOX), the query is:

  SELECT id FROM mailbox_messages WHERE user_id=? AND mailbox_id=? ORDER BY id DESC

This is executed with fetch_all(), materialising the entire result set. The Rust code then calls .skip(position).take(limit) in memory.

For a user with N messages, this loads all N IDs over the wire from SQLite even when the client requests position=0 limit=50. At 10,000 messages the overhead is still manageable, but at 100,000+ messages (a realistic long-term inbox) it becomes a full table scan across the index followed by a large Vec allocation.

Fix: push LIMIT and OFFSET into the SQL query:
  SELECT id FROM mailbox_messages WHERE user_id=? AND mailbox_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
The total count can be obtained with a separate COUNT(*) query (which SQLite can satisfy from the index without reading rows).

The composite index idx_mailbox_messages_user_mailbox on (user_id, mailbox_id) already covers this query.
